overview.title: Study in the United States
overview.description: The United States offers one of the world's most diverse higher education systems, with thousands of institutions, internationally recognised qualifications, extensive research opportunities and flexible academic pathways. Students can choose programs that match their academic background, budget and career ambitions.

quickFacts.title: Research opportunities

quickFacts.title: Flexible pathways

quickFacts.title: Global environment

visa.title: United States Student Visa Guide
visa.description: International students commonly use the F-1 student visa for academic study. The appropriate visa category depends on the institution and type of program. Applicants should follow current official U.S. immigration and consular guidance.

steps.title: Choose an eligible institution
steps.description: Research institutions and confirm that the institution is authorised to enrol international students.

steps.title: Apply for admission
steps.description: Submit academic records, English-language evidence and other documents required by the institution.

steps.title: Receive your Form I-20
steps.description: Eligible F-1 students receive a Form I-20 from their institution after meeting the necessary requirements.

steps.title: Pay applicable fees
steps.description: Review the applicable SEVIS and visa application fees and follow official payment instructions.

steps.title: Complete the visa application
steps.description: Complete the relevant application form and prepare supporting financial and academic evidence.

steps.title: Attend your visa interview
steps.description: Follow the appointment and interview instructions provided by the relevant U.S. consular service.

livingCosts.title: Estimated Monthly Living Expenses
livingCosts.description: Living expenses vary significantly by city, institution, accommodation type and personal lifestyle. Major metropolitan areas can be considerably more expensive than smaller university towns.

workRights.title: Work Opportunities in the United States
workRights.description: Student employment is subject to visa category, authorisation and applicable immigration rules. Always confirm eligibility with your institution's international student office before accepting employment.

items.title: During study
items.subtitle: Authorisation may be required
items.description: Eligible F-1 students may have limited on-campus employment opportunities. Other employment generally requires specific authorisation.

items.title: After graduation
items.subtitle: For eligible students
items.description: Optional Practical Training may be available to eligible students. Certain STEM graduates may qualify for an additional extension under applicable rules.

faqs.question: Can international students work in the United States?
faqs.answer: Eligible F-1 students may have certain on-campus employment options. Off-campus employment is subject to specific authorisation and immigration rules.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS to study in the USA?
faqs.answer: English-language requirements vary by university and program. Some institutions accept alternative English tests or offer exemptions.

faqs.question: What is Form I-20?
faqs.answer: Form I-20 is an important document issued by an eligible institution to students in relevant F-1 or M-1 student visa categories.

faqs.question: Can I apply for scholarships?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some universities offer merit-based or need-based financial assistance. Availability and eligibility vary by institution and applicant profile.

faqs.question: How much does studying in the USA cost?
faqs.answer: Tuition and living expenses vary considerably by university, program and location. Prepare a budget based on your selected institution.

faqs.question: Can I stay after graduation?
faqs.answer: Eligible graduates may explore Optional Practical Training and other applicable immigration pathways. Approval and eligibility depend on current rules.

visa.description: Applicants generally need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a licensed student sponsor and must meet current academic, English-language and financial requirements. Requirements depend on individual circumstances.

faqs.question: Can I work while studying in the UK?
faqs.answer: Some Student visa holders can work a limited number of hours during term time. Exact permissions depend on visa conditions and course eligibility.

faqs.question: How much money do I need for a UK student visa?
faqs.answer: The required funds depend on tuition fees, course location and current UKVI maintenance requirements. Check official guidance before applying.

faqs.question: Is IELTS mandatory?
faqs.answer: English-language requirements vary by university, course and visa circumstances. Some institutions accept alternative tests or exemptions.

faqs.question: Can I bring dependants?
faqs.answer: Dependant eligibility is restricted and depends on the course and applicant circumstances under current immigration rules.

faqs.question: What is the Graduate route?
faqs.answer: It is a post-study immigration route for eligible graduates. Check current GOV.UK rules for its duration and eligibility.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available for international students?
faqs.answer: Yes. Universities and external organisations offer scholarships. Funding amounts and eligibility criteria differ.
